resources.string: Checks this box, screen and sound system and suggests settings.
Reads what this box, screen and sound system support and suggests settings, each with the reason. Only suggestions based on what it could read are applied. Undo puts everything back.
Hardware video: HEVC %1$s · AV1 %2$s · VP9 %3$s · Dolby Vision %4$s
No AV1 hardware decoder: Best quality puts AV1 links last.
Puts back the settings the last Apply all changed.
Reads the TV again, for example after changing the sound system.
This screen\'s modes can\'t be read here.
This screen doesn\'t say which HDR types it shows.
This screen can switch refresh rate (%1$s Hz), so films play at their own rate without judder.
Already on. This screen can switch refresh rate (%1$s Hz).
This screen offers only %1$s Hz, so switching does nothing but can blank the picture.
This screen can switch refresh rate, so 50 Hz and 60 Hz channels play smoothly.
Decides whether the TV or this box upscales lower resolutions. Which looks better depends on your TV, so it\'s up to you.
This screen has one resolution, so this does nothing.
This screen shows Dolby Vision: Auto converts Profile 7 so it plays as Dolby Vision.
This screen shows HDR but not Dolby Vision: Auto plays Profile 7 as HDR10.
This screen has no HDR: Auto plays Profile 7 as plain HDR10 for the box to convert.
This screen shows HDR10+, so keep it.
This screen shows HDR but not HDR10+. Removing the extra data avoids flicker on some TVs.
This screen has no HDR, so this changes nothing.
Sound goes over %1$s, which carries the original formats. Forcing Dolby Digital only lowers quality.
Sound doesn\'t go over HDMI (or can\'t be read). Keep it on only if you use an optical cable.
Let the app size the buffer
Sized from this box\'s %1$s GB of memory, so it never runs out.
This box has %1$s GB of memory, too little for a large buffer.
This box has %1$s GB of memory, enough either way.
Some boxes have seek or sound sync problems with it, and that can\'t be read in advance. Turn it off if you see them.
